intro: Villa Pergia sits at the western end of Cyprus, where the Akamas peninsula begins and the coast road runs out. The Baths of Aphrodite are a five minute drive, Latchi harbour about the same, Paphos town half an hour, and the cedar forest around Kykkos Monastery forty five minutes inland.

cards.alt: The Mediterranean seen over pine and olive trees from the villa terrace
cards.title: Stunning sea views
cards.text: The terrace and both upstairs balconies look north over the treetops to open Mediterranean.

cards.alt: The turquoise shallows of the Blue Lagoon on the Akamas peninsula
cards.title: The Blue Lagoon
cards.text: Boats leave Latchi harbour each morning for the lagoon at the tip of the Akamas peninsula, clear enough to see the bottom from the deck.

cards.alt: An empty stretch of sand and shallow clear water at Latchi beach
cards.title: The beach to yourself
cards.text: Fifty metres from the door. Outside high season there are mornings when nobody else is on it. Loggerhead turtles nest along this coast.

cards.alt: The coastline shared with the neighbouring Anassa hotel
cards.title: The same beach as the Anassa
cards.text: The five star Anassa sits on the same stretch of coast. The beach itself is public.

cards.alt: View from an upstairs bedroom window across scrubland to the sea and offshore rocks
cards.title: Towards the Baths of Aphrodite
cards.text: The coast road west ends at the grotto where the myth places Aphrodite bathing, five minutes by car. It is also where the Akamas walking trails start.

cards.alt: The short path leading from the villa down to the shore
cards.title: Two minutes on foot
cards.text: The walk from the villa to the water.

cards.alt: The painted arcades and courtyard of Kykkos Monastery in the Troodos mountains
cards.title: Kykkos Monastery
cards.text: Forty five minutes inland and a thousand metres up, through cedar forest. Considerably cooler than the coast in August.

cards.alt: Roman floor mosaics in the archaeological park at Paphos
cards.title: The Paphos mosaics
cards.text: Roman floors in the harbour archaeological park, a UNESCO world heritage site, thirty minutes south.

cards.alt: A spread of small dishes making up a Cypriot fish meze
cards.title: Fish meze at the harbour
cards.text: The tavernas along Latchi harbour serve a fish meze of a dozen or more small plates. Worth booking ahead in summer.
